title: In vivio single-cell analysis of dynamic cell behaviors
text:
This project takes a multidisciplinary approach involving live microscopy, genetics and computational sciences
to address novel mechanisms that mediate cell movement and achieve tissue morphogenesis. The biological
insights and the tools developed in this project will ultimately help us understand complex tissue formation in
humans and birth defects.

title: Posttranslational regulation of macropinocytosis in pancreatic cancer
text:
The 5-year survival rate for pancreatic cancer patients is only 13%, indicating a critical need for an increased
understanding of pancreatic cancer biology in order to identify new therapeutic targets. Metabolic plasticity has
emerged as a critical mechanism for pancreatic cancer survival and therapeutic resistance. The major goal of this
proposal is to determine the role of Protein Phosphatase 2A (PP2A) in the posttranslational regulation of nutrient
scavenging pathways that contribute to PDAC survival and pancreatic cancer progression.

title: Synaptic mechanisms of auditory information processing
text:
Growing evidence shows that noise exposure and hearing loss induce profound changes in the central auditory
system from brainstem to cortex and that dysfunction of ion channels, termed channelopathies, has been linked
to many neurological disorders, including deafness and tinnitus. This project aims to study calcium permeable
ion channels and their synaptic function, and how hearing loss affects these ion channels and synaptic properties.
The research proposed here will establish a new view of the role of presynaptic calcium permeable channels in
synaptic function and their role after injury, providing the basic groundwork for future strategies for the treatment
of channelopathies and hearing disorders.

title: Role of long non-coding RNAs in modulating host immunity and pathogen survival during Orientia infection
text:
Scrub typhus, caused by Orientia tsutsugamushi, is a zoonotic disease that poses a significant risk to human
health, and more than one million infections are reported annually. Despite its impact, the molecular mechanisms
by which Orientia modulates host immune responses, induces tissue damage, and cause disease are poorly
understood; and no preventive treatments are currently available for human use. This project aims to define the
role of host non-coding RNAs in Orientia survival and pathogenesis during infection.

title: Defining epigenetic signaling to reshape pancreatic tumor microenvironment
text:
The proposed project is relevant to public health because pancreatic cancer patients have a dismal chance of
survival secondary to tumor resistance to standard chemo and immunotherapies because of the
immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment. In this proposal, we will determine how an epigenetic regulator,
KMT2D, regulates the tumor microenvironment via activin A and contributes to pancreatic cancer progression.
Our project will contribute to impactful new knowledge on the influence of tumor cell-intrinsic epigenetic
signaling on tumor microenvironment and tumor progression, which will pave the way for the clinical
development of novel tumor microenvironment-targeting treatment in combination with chemo or
immunotherapies for pancreatic cancer patients.

title: NCI National Clinical Trials Network (NCTN) - Network Lead Academic Participating Sites
text:
Relevance
As a Network Lead Academic Participating Site (LAPS), Yale University will continue to make significant
contributions to the National Cancer Institute (NCI) supported National Clinical Trials Network program. This
program has led, and will continue to lead, the development of new treatments and advances for cancer
patients, while at the same time, promoting efficiency and facilitating the prioritization of clinical research at the
national level.

title: A method for combined pulse chase labeling and super-resolution microscopy in mouse rod photoreceptor neurons
text:
The proposed research will develop a novel fluorescence-based technique for investigating the dynamics of
protein trafficking in photoreceptor cells on a subcellular scale. The development of this technique is relevant to
public health because its application will uncover critically needed details about how photoreceptor cells function
and provide the framework for understanding the molecular pathology of blinding retinal diseases. Protein
mistrafficking in photoreceptors is a pathogenic outcome of many of these diseases, which will be addressed
with this novel technique.

title: Role of m6A RNA Modifications in Microglial Dysfunction and Alzheimer's Disease Pathogenesis
text:
This project aims to investigate how RNA modifications, particularly N6-methyladenosine (m6A), in microglia
contribute to Alzheimer’s Disease (AD) and AD-related dementias (ADRD) by altering gene expression and
promoting neuroinflammation. By mapping m6A RNA modifications and using CRISPR-based approaches to
perturb key regulatory proteins, we will explore their impact on microglial functions, such as phagocytosis and
cytokine production. The findings from this research have the potential to reveal novel therapeutic targets for
developing RNA-based interventions for AD/ADRD.

title: Mesolimbic adaptations underlying altered reward sensitivity in neuropathic pain
text:
Symptoms of depression afflict between 27-75% of patients with chronic neuropathic pain; these symptoms are
associated with greater pain intensity, reduce compliance with pain management interventions and drive
reduced quality of life in patients. Despite this, there are no effective therapies for depression symptoms of
chronic pain, and these symptoms do not respond to classical antidepressant therapies. In this proposal, we
will elucidate how adaptations in the mesolimbic dopamine system drive depression symptoms in a model of
chronic neuropathic pain, which is critical for developing novel molecular targets for treating these symptoms
and ultimately for improving lives of patients with chronic neuropathic pain.

title: Spatial Multi-Omics to Profile Metabolic Pathways for Kidney Disease
text:
The KPMP Kidney Tissue Atlas is a unique resource that will form the foundation for precision medicine for the
kidney health community. Our tissue interrogation site has established the critical need for localizing molecules
linked to metabolism at a spatial level to identify pathways critical for disease understanding. With the next phase
of KPMP, we have added new expertise, improved spatial resolution, greater coverage and deep pathway
interpretative ability to bring forth new biomarkers and support precision therapeutics.

title: Functional Heterogeneity of Alveoli and the Early Response to Airborne Agents
text:
We developed the crystal ribcage, a novel imaging platform that enables real-time, high-resolution visualization
of the functioning lung, allowing us to discover a conserved, spatially organized mosaic pattern of aerosol
deposition in furthest lung regions (alveoli). We hypothesize that this pattern reflects functionally regions of
alveoli, tiles and bands, that differentially mediate early responses to inhaled agents. To test this, we will define
the anatomy and conservation of alveolar mosaicism, determine its impact on cellular gene expression and
behaviors, and evaluate how it shapes responses to injurious aerosols.

title: CRISPR-Cas-directed transposition in Tn7-like elements
text:
This project involves understanding the basic functioning of genetic elements that play a
critical role in making some bacteria pathogenic or difficult or impossible to treat because
they allow the development of drug resistance. These elements can be programed as
useful CRISPR-Cas tools for gene editing of bacteria individually or in microbiomes with
promising modifications for human therapeutic gene editing with the advances in this
proposal.

title: Engineering B cells for enhanced HIV control
text:
PROJECT NARRATIVE.
Human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) remains a considerable burden in healthcare. We are developing a new
therapy that could enhance the ability of people living with HIV to control the virus by reprograming B cells to
secrete potent anti-HIV antibodies. This technology could also be applicable to a wide range of diseases,
including cancer, and other infectious diseases.

title: Mechanisms of non-canonical T cell activation by skin commensal bacteria
text:
Our skin is covered by non-infectious bacteria that shape our immune system in ways that
significantly impact our health but are poorly understood. We propose to define how skin-
colonizing bacteria generate T cell responses without inflammation, uncovering a surprising role
for non-immune cells and bacteria-bacteria communication. This work has the potential to
translate into novel immunotherapies.

title: Regulation of Atherosclerosis by Matrikine Endotrophin
text:
The proposed research is relevant to public health because it focuses on establishing peptide endotro-
phin as a therapeutic target for coronary artery disease (CAD) and establish the mechanism by which it may
alter disease progression. We propose to utilize antibody-mediated neutralization and transgenic overexpres-
sion strategies in mice to investigate how endotrophin may signal to promote atherosclerosis. Thus, the pro-
posed research is relevant to the NHLBI mission and strategic plan to promote prevention and treatment of
cardiovascular diseases and investigate novel mechanisms important to the onset and progression of CAD.

title: In-vivo study of KSP/QRH heptapeptide dimer for detection of biliary intra-epithelial neoplasia
text:
A multi-center clinical study will be performed to evaluate the effectiveness of a new image contrast agent
to identify the cause of obstruction in the bile ducts using a flexible fiber instrument to visualize molecular
targets expressed on the tissue surface that are specific for cancer.

title: Engineering and Characterization of pH dependent Antibodies
text:
Antibodies play a vital and growing role in life science applications, such as protein therapeutics.
The research described in this proposal is designed to explore new methods to generate pH
dependent antibodies. The relevance of this project to public health is two-fold: (1) it will provide
new opportunities for the use of antibodies to preferentially target certain microenvironments,
such as that found in cancerous tumors, and (2) it will provide fundamental insight towards the
development and novel use of protein reagents for life science applications.

title: Defining features of the neoantigen-specific T cell response against a common EGFR mutation in lung cancer
text:
Mutations in our genome often give cancer cells a fitness advantage to divide and survive uncontrollably, but, by
virtue of their unique appearance in cancers, can also stimulate an anti-cancer immune response. The goal of
this project is to dissect how the most common mutation in Epidermal Growth Factor Receptor, designated
L858R, stimulates an anti-tumor immune response through activating T cells, key players of the immune system.
Knowledge gained from this project will inform the development of wide-reaching, off-the-shelf immunotherapies
for cancer patients.

title: Democratizing Detection of Hereditary Cancer Syndromes (2DETECT)
text:
Overall: NARRATIVE (Tavtigian and Del Fiol)
Early identification of individuals at high risk of hereditary cancers is critical for personalized cancer prevention
and to reduce morbidity and mortality, particularly among populations with lower previous utilization of
hereditary cancer genetics services. Further, effective implementation and dissemination of health system-level
genetic testing of hereditary cancer syndromes can improve cancer prevention, early detection, and
interception, potentially adding years—even decades—to the lives of newly detected carriers. The three
Projects in this P01 proposal attack distinct but overlapping facets of the problem, and successful completion
of these Projects will result in a decisive and generalizable enhancement in cancer genetic predisposition
testing for all populations, including those groups that have not previously been effectively reached.

title: Integrative Single Cell and Serum Biomarker Discovery for Pediatric MASLD Progression
text:
The proposed research is relevant to public health because it will provide a better understanding of how the
pediatric metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) develops and how it differs from
adult MASLD. The project is relevant to NIH’s mission because it will help reduce morbidity due to pediatric
MASLD.
